summary: Raffaele Pettazzoni (1883–1959) worked in religious studies and history and archaeology. He earned a Ph.D. from the University of Bologna and a PD from Sapienza University of Rome, later holding professorships at Bologna (1914–1922) and Sapienza (1923–1958).
Raffaele Torella (born 1950) is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Raniero Gnoli. He served as a faculty member at Sapienza University of Rome from circa 1976 to 2020.
Raffaello Orlando is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Princeton University in 1981, studying under doctoral supervisor Denis Twitchett.

Raghu Ananthanarayanan works in philosophy and religious studies. A post-graduate in engineering from IIT Madras, he studied under Tirumalai Krishnamacharya and T. K. V. Desikachar, later teaching at Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram and visiting IIM Ahmedabad in 2010.

Raghu Vira (1902–1963) was a scholar in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. Educated at University of the Punjab and Leiden University under Willem Caland, he directed the International Academy of Indian Culture from 1934.

Raghunath Damodar Karmarkar (1893–1964) worked in Indology and philosophy. He served as Principal of Sir Parashurambhau College and as Director of the Post-Graduate and Research Department at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute.
Raghunath Giri was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Vamacharana Bhattacharya. He served as a section head at Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith.

Rahul Parson is an Indologist who earned his PhD from the University of California, Berkeley (2004–2012). He held assistant professorships at the University of Colorado Boulder (2016–2020) and UC Berkeley (2021).

Rahul Peter Das (born 1954) specializes in Indology and linguistics. After studying at Hamburg under Klaus Ludwig Janert and Albrecht Wezler, he taught at Hamburg, Bonn, and Groningen before becoming a professor at MLU Halle-Wittenberg (circa 1994–2020).

Rahul Sankrityayan (1893–1963) worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He held a teaching position at Vidyalankara Pirivena in 1927 and taught Sanskrit and held a professorship at Saint Petersburg State University (1937, 1945–1947).

Raimo Anttila (1935–2023) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Yale under doctoral supervisor Warren Crawford Cowgill and held posts at UCLA (1965) and the University of Helsinki (1971–1976).

Raimon Panikkar (1918–2010) was a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Madrid, Rome, Mysore, and BHU, and held teaching posts at Complutense University of Madrid, Harvard, and UC Santa Barbara (1971–1978).

Raimond Gaita (born 1946) is a philosopher educated at Melbourne and Leeds. He served as Professor of Moral Philosophy at King's College London (1977–2011) and Foundation Professor of Philosophy at Australian Catholic University (1993–2011).

Raj Ballav Panda works in Indology. He completed an M.Sc. at Centurion University, degrees at Rajendra University, and a Ph.D. at Banaras Hindu University in 2022, holding posts at Rajendra University (2018) and Klorofeel School (2022).
Raja Pathak is an Indologist who completed his Ph.D. at Banaras Hindu University (2014–2020) and holds a post at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

Raja Ram Shastri (1904–1991) was an Indology scholar and Lok Sabha member (circa 1971–1977). He was attested in 1976 as Chairman of the Managing Committee at Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri National Sanskrit University.

Rajan Gurukkal (born 1948) works in history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Calicut and JNU, he became Director of the School of Social Sciences at Mahatma Gandhi University (1988) and Sundararajan Visiting Professor at IISc (2012–2016).

Rajan Khatiwoda (born 1984) is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He earned his PhD at Heidelberg University (2013–2017) and held positions at the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities and Heidelberg University (2017–2026).
Rajaram Hegde is a scholar of history, archaeology, and religious studies. In 2010, he was attested as Director at Kuvempu University and Director of the Centre for the Study of Local Cultures.
Rajat Pal is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at Gurukula Kangri Vishwavidyalaya and is pursuing a Ph.D. at the Indian Institute of Technology Madras (2022–2026).
